claim_title: Three of five exercises nonclustered indexes are leading-column redundant - cleanup candidate, NOT justified for action now
summary: The size/fragmentation/rowcount numbers reproduce exactly, but the central claim - that three indexes are leading-column redundant (strict prefixes) - is mathematically FALSE for all three. No index in the exercises set is a prefix of another. The claim's own operational conclusion (do nothing) is coincidentally harmless, but the finding is built on a fabricated structural premise and must not be recorded.

reproduced_exactly.note: Claimed sizes 1.13/3.66/2.46/1.40 MB and total 19.92 MB match dm_db_partition_stats used_page_count*8/1024.0 within rounding. All fragmentation < 11% confirmed. These facts are REAL.

refutation.method: sys.index_columns + sys.columns, is_included_column=0, ordered by key_ordinal; then a literal LIKE 'prefix%' test in T-SQL, plus manual column-by-column comparison.
why_false: idx_exercises_lesson_order (lesson_id, order_index): 2nd key col is order_index, but both candidate parents have exercise_type as their 2nd col. Column ORDER differs -> not a prefix.

idx_exercises_type (exercise_type): its only col is exercise_type, but idx_exercises_lesson_type_order LEADS with lesson_id. A single-column index is never a prefix of an index that starts with a different column.
None of the five nonclustered indexes is a strict leading-column prefix of any other in this set.
refutation.included_columns_ignored_by_claim: idx_exercises_lesson_type_order carries INCLUDE (correct_answer, difficulty). The claim treats index key columns only and does not mention INCLUDEs; irrelevant to prefix status (included cols never affect key-prefix), but the claim's omission shows it was not derived from sys.index_columns.

all_indexes_are_actually_used.source: sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats since last SQL Server restart
all_indexes_are_actually_used.note: Every one of the five nonclustered indexes has user_seeks > 0. idx_exercises_lesson_order (231 seeks) and idx_exercises_type (24 seeks) are demonstrably serving real query shapes, further contradicting 'redundant'.

evidence: findByLessonIdOrderByOrderIndexAsc -> WHERE lesson_id=? ORDER BY order_index  => idx_exercises_lesson_order
findAdminPage filters on exercise_type alone (with :type IS NULL OR ...) => idx_exercises_type
query_shapes_confirming_distinct_purpose.conclusion: Each index backs a distinct, real access path. There is no prefix redundancy to clean up.

file_reference_check: Claim cites src/main/java/com/datn/engflow/model/entity/Exercise.java. That file contains NO @Index / @Table(indexes=...) annotations (grep for 'Index' returns nothing). The indexes were not declared in the entity, so the cited file is not the origin of these objects; a schema-diff/SQL script is. Minor but shows the claim's provenance is loose.
severity_assessment: Claimed LOW. Because the premise is false, there is no cleanup candidate and no LOW-severity issue to carry. Correct disposition: DROP the finding (INVALID). The claim's own conclusion ('does NOT justify action') happens to align with reality only by accident - it says do nothing because redundant indexes aren't hurting, whereas the truth is there are no redundant indexes at all.
probe_artefact_check: Not a probe artefact: this is a pure catalog/source inspection, no HTTP, no rate limit, no DOM involved. Numbers are stable and reproducible via sqlrun.py.
